sug_intentionOvercommit_lead.message: Three or four things you actually finish beats ten you meant to.

sug_intentionOvercommit_text1.message: Set fewer. One thing that must happen, and two that would be good, is a full day for most people.

sug_intentionOvercommit_text2.message: Make each one small enough to finish in a sitting — "draft the email" rather than "sort out the application".

sug_intentionOvercommit_text3.message: Move the ones that keep rolling over into a single "someday" note, so they stop reappearing as today's failure.

sug_noBreaks_lead.message: Rest that never gets logged tends to be rest that never happens.

sug_noBreaks_text1.message: Put breaks on a timer, so stopping isn't a decision you have to make while concentrating.

sug_noBreaks_text2.message: Take the break away from the screen entirely — a walk, food, or anything that isn't another window.

sug_noBreaks_text3.message: If you're already resting but not logging it, log it. A day that reads as sixteen unbroken hours isn't the day you had.

sug_peakHoursUnprotected_lead.message: The hour you're best in is worth defending before anything else gets to claim it.

sug_peakHoursUnprotected_text1.message: Block it in whatever calendar other people can see, so the time is taken before someone else takes it.

sug_peakHoursUnprotected_text2.message: Silence everything for that hour, rather than relying on not looking.

sug_peakHoursUnprotected_text3.message: Start the hardest thing of the day in that window, not the easiest. The easy work will survive being done at a worse hour; the hard work often won't.

sug_peakHoursUnprotected_text4.message: If you can, change where you are for that hour. A different room or a library does more than most software.

sug_distractionTrend_lead.message: Rising distraction is usually a friction problem rather than a willpower one — the aim is to make the easy thing slightly harder.

sug_distractionTrend_text1.message: Block the sites that take the time, but only during the hours you actually want to work — an all-day block tends to get switched off entirely.

sug_distractionTrend_text2.message: Add a pause before the app opens, instead of blocking it. A few seconds of friction removes most of the opening-it-without-deciding-to.

sug_distractionTrend_text3.message: Make the phone boring for a while rather than forbidden.

sug_distractionTrend_text4.message: Put the phone in another room while you work. Unglamorous, free, and more reliable than anything you can install on the device you're trying to avoid.

sug_distractionTrend_text5.message: Replace rather than remove — decide what the time goes to instead, or it tends to find its way back.

sug_coverageDecline_lead.message: Logging less is usually the first sign of a stretch going badly — and the thing that makes it hard to see how badly.

sug_coverageDecline_text1.message: Log at two or three fixed points in the day rather than reconstructing it at midnight. Daily Dial's own reminders (Settings → Reminders) exist for this.

sug_coverageDecline_text2.message: Log roughly rather than not at all. An approximate day is worth far more than a blank one, and you can always sharpen it.

sug_coverageDecline_text3.message: Use "The day, end to end" below the dial to fill gaps in a couple of minutes — the rows are already there, they just need words.

sug_coverageDecline_text4.message: If it's stopped being worth the effort, that's worth knowing too. A tracker you resent is one you'll abandon.

sug_untrackedLifeArea_lead.message: What isn't a category can't show up in any of these numbers — and what doesn't show up is easy to let slide.

sug_untrackedLifeArea_text1.message: Rename a category you don't use to cover something that's missing — time with other people, exercise, sleep, or anything you'd want to be honest with yourself about (Settings → Categories).

sug_untrackedLifeArea_text2.message: Give it a neutral weight rather than a productive one. The point is to see it, not to score it.

sug_untrackedLifeArea_text3.message: Once it's a category, the goals and History trends you already have will do the rest without any further effort.

sug_targetMismatch_lead.message: The target is a setting, not a verdict. It's worth moving when it stops describing you.

sug_targetMismatch_text1.message: If you clear it most days, raise it. A target you always meet stops telling you anything — the score flattens out near the top, where it can no longer tell a good day from an ordinary one.

sug_targetMismatch_text2.message: If you rarely come close, lower it. An unreachable target doesn't make anyone do more; it just makes the number feel like it's about someone else, and a number like that gets ignored.
